title: Establish atomic token contracts and autolayout resilience pipeline
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: Reduce library fragility by converting legacy surface tokens and component-level overrides into a set of small, well-documented atomic token contracts, and implement an automated autolayout resilience pipeline that detects and fixes common layout regressions for tables, charts, and button groups before publish.

Background: Over the last year we've accumulated token aliases and ad-hoc component overrides to meet feature requests quickly. This has increased publish risk: small token changes cause widespread visual regressions, and several teams have reported table row spacing drift and misaligned chart legends after library updates. Publishing is currently a manual gating flow with no automated remediation for typical auto-layout issues.

Scope:
- Identify and canonicalize a minimal set of atomic tokens for spacing, typography, radius, and color intent relevant to controls (buttons), data surfaces (tables, charts), and layout primitives.
- Replace component-level numeric overrides in primary button, button group, table row, and chart legend components with references to the new atomic token contracts.
- Implement a Figma plugin CI job (via existing publish pipeline) that runs a lint-and-fix step to detect common autolayout anti-patterns (fixed padding on nested frames, mixed axis constraints, empty-frame spacing) and propose fixes or automatically apply safe changes.
- Add clear migration notes and a short migration guide + rollout checklist in Confluence and a quick video walkthrough for internal consumers.

Out of scope: Full redesign of components, global token rename across unrelated libraries, or automated refactors that change visual intent beyond ±1px or color deltas above the defined tolerance.

Why this approach: Atomic token contracts reduce cognitive load for consumers and make the intent explicit (e.g., spacing.control-compact vs spacing.card). The autolayout resilience pipeline reduces human review time and prevents regressions that are frequent in table/chart updates.

Acceptance criteria:
- A canonical token map (CSV) exists mapping legacy tokens to new atomic contracts and is documented in Confluence.
- Primary button, button group, table row, and chart legend components have been refactored to reference only atomic tokens (no numeric layer overrides) in the Figma library file.
- Publish pipeline includes a lint job that flags at least 80% of the common autolayout issues we saw in the last three releases and automatically fixes safe issues.
- Migration notes and a short walkthrough video are published and linked from the library release notes.

Rollout plan:
1) Spike (1 week): inventory legacy tokens and component overrides; build token mapping proposal.
2) Refactor (2 weeks): update components in a branch file, run internal smoke tests across two consumer teams.
3) Pipeline work (2 weeks parallel): add lint-and-fix plugin to publish CI; validate on branch file.
4) Canary publish + feedback (1 week): publish to QA library, gather issues, iterate.
5) Full publish + communication: publish and send migration guide + video.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Automatic fixes could change visual intent. Mitigation: keep conservative auto-fix rules and require human approval for fixes that change >1px or exceed color delta thresholds.
- Risk: Consumers rely on numeric overrides in their local files. Mitigation: include compatibility notes and a migration mapping; add a quick script to help replace deprecated tokens in instances where possible.

QA checklist:
- Visual diffs run for core viewports comparing old vs new library for buttons, tables, charts.
- Verify no broken instances in the top 30 product files listed in our consumer inventory.
- Confirm publish pipeline lint flags are actionable and have clear guidance in PRs.

Notes for engineers: Keep the code for the Figma plugin in the existing infra repo (infra/figma-pipeline). PR should include a README and tests for the auto-fix heuristics. When creating the canonical token map, attach a CSV with columns: legacy_token, new_contract, rationale, affected_components.
